source.name: Form fields inside a disabled fieldset must not be treated as tabbable, so a focus-trapped dialog focuses its first usable field
source.scope: Real upstream bug (https://github.com/focus-trap/tabbable/issues/413) at cc8b7b2bc4319b672d0e6053b34c732168dd035c. Blind to the maintainers' fix 1d5fcb51d9eb21994c82a2f03010bc0d017cfff2; routing auto.

guards.title: Escape closes the address dialog and returns focus
guards.goal: Escape dismisses the dialog and focus returns to the trigger

plan.root_cause: The focus trap's default option delayInitialFocus:true defers setting initial focus to the next tick, leaving focus on the triggering button after the dialog opens and causing the assertion that focus should be on #street to fail.
plan.repair_strategy: Disable the delayInitialFocus option when creating the focus trap so that initial focus is set synchronously upon activation, moving focus to the first focusable field (#street) immediately.

edits.before: const trap = createFocusTrap('#address-dialog', { onDeactivate: () => { backdrop.hidden = true; } });
edits.after: const trap = createFocusTrap('#address-dialog', { onDeactivate: () => { backdrop.hidden = true; }, delayInitialFocus: false });

plan.expected_accessibility_effect: When the address dialog is opened via keyboard, focus moves to the first usable field (the street address input) allowing immediate interaction.
functional_risks: Change in focus timing could affect any code that relies on the delayed focus behavior, but no such usage is present in the provided source.
verification_requirements: After pressing Enter on the #open button, the #address-dialog is visible and #street receives focus.
Pressing Escape still closes the dialog and returns focus to the #open button.
Entering a street address and pressing Save updates the status correctly and closes the dialog.

plan.root_cause: The focus trap's default `delayInitialFocus: true` defers initial focus to the next event loop tick, and the automatic first-tabbaable-node selection may not resolve correctly due to timing or visibility of the dialog. This leaves focus on the triggering button (#open) after the dialog opens, causing the keyboard focus assertion to fail.
plan.repair_strategy: Modify the `createFocusTrap` call in index.html to disable delayed initial focus and explicitly set the initial focus target to the street input (#street). This ensures focus moves synchronously to the intended field when the dialog is activated via keyboard.

edits.before: const trap = createFocusTrap('#address-dialog', { onDeactivate: () => { backdrop.hidden = true; } });
edits.after: const trap = createFocusTrap('#address-dialog', { onDeactivate: () => { backdrop.hidden = true; }, delayInitialFocus: false, initialFocus: '#street' });

plan.expected_accessibility_effect: When the address dialog is opened via keyboard (Enter on #open), focus moves immediately to the street address input (#street), allowing the user to type the address without an extra Tab press.
functional_risks: Explicit initialFocus overrides the library's automatic first-tabbaable-node logic, but the street input is the intended first field in the dialog.
No other focus traps or focus-dependent code are present in the provided source.
verification_requirements: After pressing Enter on the #open button, the #address-dialog becomes visible and #street receives focus.
Pressing Escape closes the dialog and returns focus to the #open button.
Entering a street address and pressing Save updates the status text to "Delivering to 12 Elm Street." and closes the dialog.
The independent task (Escape closes dialog) continues to pass.
